title: Spunk
focus: courage and guilt in a small community

teacherSummary.text: In an Eatonville store, men watch big Spunk Banks walk off with Lena, wife of timid Joe Kanty. Shamed, Joe attacks Spunk with a razor and is shot dead. A black bobcat haunts Spunk, who believes it is Joe. At the sawmill Spunk is pushed onto the saw and dies, saying Joe pushed him. The town gossips about who will court Lena next.

segments.activity: Model the close reading of the anchor quotation using the written think-aloud below.
segments.script: First, meaning. I read “Ah b'leeve Joe pushed 'im mahself” slowly and put it in my own words: One of the porch-sitters says he believes dead Joe pushed Spunk into the saw. Next, craft. I notice the dialect and the calm tone about a ghost, as if it is common sense. The strongest word is “pushed”: it gives the dead man action, which makes Joe's revenge real to the community. Then, effect. Why does the speaker believe Joe pushed Spunk? My answer: The town reads Spunk's death as justice from Joe's spirit; Hurston shows folk belief as the community's way of making sense of violence.
